Name: Guildford Arts
Role/Bio: Hosting / curating an exhibition. Networking & PR. Guildford Arts belief is that the ARTS are an essential component to enrich people’s lives and that culturally speaking, the ARTS allow for the expression of creative exercise and teach tolerance for diversity. The ARTS also hold great financial and economic benefit for Guildford, as it attracts visitors and gives Guildford a strong identity. For many years, Guildford Arts have been committed to opening the world of the ARTS for everyone, connecting people to the ARTS and to each other. The social aspect of membership is intrinsic in everything that they do. They want to connect people together that have a passion for the ARTS and ultimately work to create a better, healthier and more connected society.

Name: Griffin and Jones
Role/Bio: One of the main artists at Guildford Fringe Festival. They are supplying a relaxed performance during the festival.Griffin and Jones are The Pioneers of Slapdash Magic! What does that mean? Well… These award-winning idiots have been touring the UK, wowing audiences with their own brand of homemade miracles since 2011. Fusing razor sharp, ‘machine-gun patter’ [The Reviews Hub], a uniquely bizarre and irreverent sense of humour, a joyously inclusive party atmosphere, and some of the most impressive, impossible magic you are likely to see, an evening in the company of these surprisingly good magicians is one you are not likely to forget in a hurry!

Name: Opera on the Balcony
Role/Bio: The Guildhall becomes the stage for a free evening of Opera on the Balcony for the 4th year and is very much ‘back by popular demand’! Opera on the Balcony, performed by leading UK opera singers from the balcony of The Guildhall. Performers have been prevented from singing live for so long so this, in some ways, is the industries Independence Day! Yes, they are back with a vengeance and will be bringing you arias and duets from well-loved composers such as Puccini, Verdi, Mozart, Lehar and many more. They’ll sing freely & joyously into the warm evening air and you can sit back, enjoy a chilled glass of something from the Guildford Fringe bar and let the music wash over you and blow away the isolation of this past year!

Role/Bio: One of the main artists at Guildford Fringe Festival. Name: Apollo Theatre Company
Role/Bio: Delivering a performance with BSL integration.Apollo Theatre Company was founded in 2010 by Tim Astley upon graduating from the Guildford School of Acting.Tim trained at the Guildford School of Acting and, shortly after graduating in 2010, founded Apollo Theatre Company and made his directorial debut with their first production, Sir Harold Pinter’s The Dumb Waiter. The following year he directed Apollo’s first touring production, Dennis Potter’s Blue Remembered Hills, followed by the 75th Anniversary UK Tour of Thornton Wilder’s Our Town and Nina Bawden’s Carrie’s War in which he also played the role of Billy. Alongside his wife, Amy, Tim created Apollo Theatre Company’s first original production, Keep the Home Fires Burning, which told the oft-forgotten roles women played in World War II. He also directed another original piece, The Code Breaker, which celebrated the life and work of Alan Turing. A lifelong fan of radio comedy, Tim fulfilled a long-time dream in 2015 when he produced and directed the 50th Anniversary Tour of his all-time favourite radio show, Round the Horne which toured the UK three times and played for eight weeks in London’s Museum of Comedy. Following this wonderful experience, Tim collaborated with Colin Elmer, who played Kenneth Williams in the show, to create an original production about the great man. Entitled Cult Figure, the production toured the country in 2017 and 2018. Bitten by the bug of recreating comedy classics, Tim produced and directed another classic radio comedy to the stage in The Goon Show and yet another, Hancock’s Half Hour in 2019.

Role/Bio: Nick directs Guildford Fringe Theatre Company LTD which includes the Theatre Company, Guildford Fringe Festival and Gag House Comedy Clubs and produces professional work throughout the year.Their work includes producing theatre, comedy clubs, cabarets, family pantomimes, adult panto’s and Guildford Fringe Festival as well as assisting with town centre and community events. The organisation was set up in 2012 (and incorporated in 2014) to bring a different kind of arts offering to Guildford and they do this by using unconventional venues and putting on events that the mainstream theatres probably wouldn’t. They believe the arts should be for everyone, from every background. The goal is to make this a reality.
